summary: Every winter Lahore's smog is not mainly new pollution; it is the same year-round smoke trapped close to the ground. In winter the ground cools fast at night, a layer of warmer air sits above the cold air (a temperature inversion) and acts like a lid, the layer in which smoke can mix and spread shrinks sharply, and winds over eastern Punjab are often very weak. Under this lid, emissions from vehicles, industry and brick kilns build up, and late-season crop-residue burning around Lahore (on both sides of the border) adds a big seasonal burst. In November 2024 Lahore recorded its worst readings ever, and Punjab closed schools across many districts. What helps is cutting the sources (crop burning, dirty vehicles and kilns), because the weather lid cannot be removed.
audience: Lahore and Punjab residents aged 15-35 who live through smog every winter and wonder why it returns each year

facts.fact: A temperature inversion is when warmer air sits above colder air near the ground; it stops the normal upward movement of air and acts like a lid that traps pollutants near the surface.
In winter the height of the atmospheric layer into which Lahore's pollution can disperse drops sharply, which is one of the main reasons air quality worsens in winter.
From November to January, eastern Punjab often has very weak winds (below about 1.5 metres per second) and deep inversions that prevent natural ventilation of the air.
facts.source: KFUPM study of winter fog episodes over Punjab

facts.fact: An emissions inventory based on 2020-21 data put transport at about 35 percent and crop-residue burning at about 33 percent of Lahore's PM2.5 emissions.
Between 37 and 63 percent of crop-fire detections within 100 km of Lahore on the Pakistani side came after 1 November in each season from 2019 to 2025, the same time the mixing layer becomes shallow.
Lahore's air pollution is a year-round problem; winter weather and crop burning make an existing baseline much worse.
Seasonal winds can carry smoke from crop burning in Indian Punjab across the border to Pakistan, so smog is a shared regional problem.

Peer-reviewed research concludes crop-residue burning and motor vehicles have greatly increased the frequency and intensity of smog events, with weather (humidity, wind, dew point) deciding how bad each episode gets.
facts.source: Majeed et al., Frontiers in Sustainable Cities (2024)

facts.fact: In early November 2024 Lahore's air quality index exceeded 1,000, a record for Pakistan, and primary schools in Lahore were closed for a week from 4 November.
Punjab later closed schools and colleges across 18 districts from 7 to 17 November 2024 and set up a smog war room.
Because the weather lid cannot be removed, lasting improvement depends on cutting the sources: crop-residue burning, smoky vehicles, and industrial and brick-kiln emissions.
facts.source: Frontiers 2024; Hamari Hawa report via Dawn

avoid: Blaming only India or only farmers; sources differ on the shares and the problem is shared
Quoting a single record AQI number as exact (monitors disagree: AP said over 1,000, others cited higher local readings)
Medical advice or specific mask/health claims
Calling smog 'fog'; fog is water droplets, smog is pollution (they often mix)
